reported_context.description: User reported that selecting/targeting an enemy in the current combat test did not make the character face it.
reported_context.user_test_timestamp: unknown; no build or test timestamp was supplied
reported_context.selection_vs_attack: The source does not turn merely because a target was selected. Facing is expected after an attack state is admitted and while that state remains active.

visual_evidence.reference: Dungeon Hunter 2 v1.0.3 Part 1, local decoded frames from the original video

frames.observation: A red target ring is visible around the Bog Moth while the player is in a sword-strike pose. This establishes target selection concurrent with combat; it does not show what selection alone does.

The player and enemy are in changed poses in the next sampled frame, with damage text over the enemy. This is consistent with continued combat presentation, but these half-second samples do not establish exact turn rate or continuous per-frame heading.

visual_evidence.inference: The visuals support checking target-facing during an admitted attack. The frames do not prove immediate rotation on target selection or quantify the rotation interpolation.

selection_and_admission: Character::Ctrl_Click 0x3addc8 selects an eligible Character by whole CharAI::AI_SetTarget(target,false); the recovered movement-controller audit confirms selection does not run its movement tail and this path does not call LookAt.

v2Controller::Cmd_Attack 0x405b04 checks global blocked and local locked unless forced, then dispatches controllable virtual+0x38. Character::Ctrl_Attack 0x3ad87c calls CharAI::AI_DoMeleeAttack 0x3d01ac with mode=false.
CSAttack::OnFocus 0x3c404c selects the source moving/static Attack bank based on previous state and authored stance masks. It does not itself establish the per-frame target turn.
facing_during_attack: CSAttack::OnUpdate 0x3c14f8 calls GameObject::LookAt(owner,target) on every Attack-state update, then refreshes attack speed only if the property changed.

CSAttack::OnEvent 0x3c1288 handles event26: if Character target+0x408 exists, it obtains GameObject::GetTargetPosition and calls GameObject::LookAt; with no target, only the ranged-weapon plus owner-byte+0x1b5 branch uses SetHeadingDirection.

CharAI::_OnAnimStepBegin 0x3d4204 dispatches Attack state5 to _OnAnimStepBegin_Attack 0x3d4044. At depth0 that consumer raises Character event0x1a with the step word; depth1 calls controller Cmd_LookAt(owner+0x408). CharAI event routing then reaches the active state handler. Thus step-begin facing is additional to CSAttack::OnUpdate, not a target-selection side effect.

v2Controller::Cmd_LookAt(GameObject*) 0x4052bc applies its original global/local/forced gates and dispatches virtual+0x14. Character::Ctrl_LookAt 0x3ad9ac reaches GameObject::LookAt; the recovered target-facing proof documents that LookAt updates desired heading and source rotation integration publishes the bounded physical Euler turn.
source_logic.turning_math: CombatSession::Impl::turn in port/windows-foundation/combat_session.cpp:729-745 uses dh2_nav_look_towards to derive the live target heading and dh2_actor_update_rotation with the resolved rotation modifier and integer milliseconds. It publishes the resulting rotation to ActorState::transform.rotation[2]; it does not snap.

current_path_finding.selection: CombatSession::update cycles target at combat_session.cpp:1382. This is selection-only and currently leaves facing unchanged, consistent with recovered selection logic.
current_path_finding.attack_admission: Diagnostic attack admission turns before request in diagnostic_attack_body at combat_session.cpp:848. The source-combo bridge also calls turn when attack_set_attack_state is reached at combat_session.cpp:933. The controller gates and source attack owner still control whether that service is reached.
current_path_finding.held_attack_gap_and_fix: Before the root fix, the generic frame's attack-facing turn was an `else if`, skipped for input.attack=true. Root now calls turn for every active attacking ActorState at combat_session.cpp:1395 independent of held input. Entry::rotationUpdateSerial and the update_serial guard in turn() ensure admission plus active-update paths consume at most one dt budget per frame; restore resets that serial. The feature regression passes this path for both real player profiles.
current_path_finding.event26_gap: The source event26 path is documented above; this feature regression validates the reusable bounded per-frame update and does not claim the retained attack sequence dispatches a new event26 state callback.
current_path_finding.host_rotation_overwrite: CombatSession::update writes the caller-provided facing into ActorState at combat_session.cpp:1369 before command/turn processing. The existing combo test feeds the prior ActorState rotation back on subsequent frames (runtime_player_combo_chain_v1_tests.cpp:294-296), so stale host facing does not explain that fixture's missing held-input turn. A production caller that keeps passing an older constant would independently erase the prior frame's rotation and must feed back the published transform.

current_fixture_and_verification.fixture: features/combat/runtime_player_combo_chain_v1_tests.cpp uses actual authored KnightPlayerBase player data and a Swamp_LizadMan_Type1 source actor. The current fixture puts the target at (0,-100,0) with initial yaw0; the recovered navigation heading formula makes this cardinal bearing heading0, so it is aligned and is NOT meaningful facing regression evidence. Selection, target_id and selectedactor are asserted separately. This is a Knight profile fixture, not a Rogue profile fixture.
current_fixture_and_verification.result: PASS existing combo/selection assertions; this test does not assert target-facing or compare rendered pose heading with a source target heading. It is not a target-facing regression result.
current_fixture_and_verification.build_isolation: The focused runner linked copied archives from `.local-inputs/windows-foundation-build` in `.local-inputs/target-facing-20261010-private-build`; shared build outputs were not written.
current_fixture_and_verification.new_focused_regression: features/combat/target_facing_regression_tests.cpp and run_target_facing_regression_tests.ps1 cover actual KnightPlayerBase and RoguePlayerBase source profiles with actual Swamp_LizadMan_Type1 actors, selection-only no-turn, positive-dt admission compared exactly with one source dh2_actor_update_rotation step (proving no double advance and no snap), held active attack tracking compared with subsequent source rotation-kernel steps toward +pi/4 and then a live retarget at -pi/4, plus unchanged target identity, attack ownership/generation and combat RNG.
current_fixture_and_verification.runner_result: PASS KnightPlayerBase and RoguePlayerBase each tracked the actual same-session Swamp_LizadMan_Type1 target from +pi/4 toward -pi/4 during held attack input; selection stayed yaw0; generation and RNG were preserved.

expected_behavior_and_minimal_fix.expected: Target selection alone updates the selected target and should not force a turn. Once the source Attack state is admitted, facing tracks the live target through the source desired-heading and bounded rotation policy while the actor remains in Attack; no unconditional turn should be added to moving, casting, hurt or dead actors.
expected_behavior_and_minimal_fix.candidate_core_owner: Integration lead/root owns port/windows-foundation/combat_session.cpp. This is outside the permitted feature-only write scope, so no implementation was made.
expected_behavior_and_minimal_fix.minimal_seam: Root implemented a bounded turn for each active attacking frame regardless of held input, while a per-frame rotationUpdateSerial prevents admission and active-frame paths from applying the same elapsed budget twice. The actor's live target_id remains authoritative; existing target/actor/range validity gates remain in turn(). The separate authored event26 callback remains an additional source step-boundary path and is not claimed wired by this regression.
expected_behavior_and_minimal_fix.alternative_integration_check: The Windows main render path statically consumes ActorState heading: after Session updates it passes the player actor rotation to ActorMovement::setFacingRadians (main.cpp:2589); the source-heading branch copies actor.rotation into sourceVisualYaw for the nonmoving player (main.cpp:2619); player actorWorld uses that published source yaw or the motor facing (main.cpp:2700); NPC placement uses live ActorState rotation (main.cpp:2724). Static review found no stale-facing overwrite in those presentation consumers. The Android main renderer has a separate prince_runtime source heading path and does not call CombatSession::turn. GUI confirmation is still required.

focused_regression_plan: For both actual KnightPlayerBase and RoguePlayerBase profile rows, place the player at (0,0,0), a real Swamp_LizadMan_Type1 target at (100,-100,0), and initialize player yaw0. The recovered `navigation_heading.cpp` formula `atan(x/-y)` yields desired heading +π/4 for this bearing. Assert targetSelect changes target_id/selectedactor but not yaw.

Admit an attack at dt0 and assert no instant yaw snap. During the active source Attack pose, continue delivering attack input across positive-dt frames while feeding the just-published player rotation back as the next facing argument; assert rotation advances boundedly toward +π/4 under the source rotation speed, and the rendered CharacterVisual root/model orientation corresponds to the same actor transform.

Repeat with a second non-collinear target at (-100,-100,0), whose desired heading is -π/4, retarget during an active swing, and verify the next active frame follows the live target without changing actor identity or selection bookkeeping.
Negative cases: no active attack (selection only), moving, cast/state7, hurt, dead actor, invalid/dead/out-of-range target; assert no attack-facing turn outside original gates.
uncertainties: The exact reported test build, class, held-input sequence, target bearing, and observation timestamp were not supplied; all remain unknown.
